Spectre''' is a [[minion]] [[spell]] [[active skill|skill]] that summons a defeated enemy as an allied [[minion]]. '''Reading [[Guide:How to avoid losing your spectres]] before investing in any very expensive ones is recommended.''' ==Skill functions and interactions== *'''Monster types''': Raised Spectres typically retain the basic abilities they had in life, though not any properties gained from monster rarity or [[monster modifiers]]. Additionally, some monsters may have modified stats, behaviour, or skills as Spectres. For example, Necromancers will still cast curses but not raise minions. ** Some monsters like Reanimators and Spectral Tacticians do retain the ability to summon their own minions (Zombies and Raging Spirits, respectively). Minions' minions are not the player's minions, and will only be affected by Minion-specific stats on support gems and stats that affect allies, like Auras. *'''[[Support gems]]''': Raise Spectre can be supported by many different types of support gems, but not all of them may be beneficial depending on the type of Spectres raised. Minion-specific support gems will work on every type of spectre, but a more specific gem such as {{il|Greater Multiple Projectiles Support}} will only affect spectres with [[projectile]] abilities. ** Note that support gems grant stats to minions globally, not separately to each of their skills. This means an attack-only support like {{il|Withering Touch Support}} can modify spellcaster spectres, as the added stats are ''not'' limited to attacks.https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1eJt-Fx3reY **Minions do not [[snapshot]] their support gems: they gain stats from gems that are currently linked to the Raise Spectre gem, not gems linked when a specific minion was raised. A player can summon minions without certain support gems (e.g. to lower the cost, or to avoid uncontrolled targeting by {{il|Spell Echo Support}}) and then fully link the skill afterward. **{{Il|Lifetap Support}} will affect both the cost of the skill and of minions' own skills. This can help certain spectres that have mana costs, though this is only the case for very old monsters. Monster skills are normally regulated by [[cooldown]]s.https://discord.com/channels/174993814845521922/174994219390337024/1177472328960065569 *'''Corpse targeting''': Holding down the corpse targeting toggle (defaults to the "A" key) makes it easier to choose a corpse to raise. Note that you must continue targeting the corpse while raising the spectre. If you let go of your corpse target button you may raise a different spectre. *'''Monster level''': Spectre level is based on the level of the '''Raise Spectre''' skill gem. The level of the corpse it raises does not matter. *{{il|Desecrate}} can be used to generate corpses to raise as spectres. See {{il|Desecrate}} for more details. *'''Death''': When a spectre dies, it turns into a spectre orb that holds its soul. In this form, the spectre cannot attack, use skills, be damaged, or be interacted with in any meaningful way. When you leave the instance, the spectre will be revived. An icon indicating the number of dead spectres will appear on you buff bar. * '''Loss Protection''': Raised spectres persist after logout or disconnection and conditionally persist if you lose your spectres as by removing the gem or missing [[attribute]] requirements. ** '''Protection Condition 1.''' If you lose your spectres in [[town]] and restore the gem or [[attribute]] requirements while in town, your spectres will be automatically raised. ** '''Protection Condition 2.''' If you lose your spectres in [[town]], but don't restore the gem or [[attribute]] requirements while in town, corpses of your [[Corpse item]] spectres will spawn at the entrance of the next hostile [[area]] you enter. The corpses will remain in the zone until either the owner raises these corpses or the [[instance]] expires. ** '''Protection Condition 3.''' If you lose your spectres in your [[hideout]], corpses of your [[Corpse item]] spectres will spawn immediately in your [[hideout]]. ** '''Protection Condition 4.''' If your spectres die in a hostile [[area]], your spectres will transform into "Orb Spectres" that cannot use skills and cannot be targeted. They will automatically transform back to their original form upon entering a new area or instance. ** '''Loss Condition.''' If you lose your spectres in a hostile [[area]] such as by removing the gem or missing [[attribute]] requirements, your spectres will despawn. Most spectres are still retained in the spectre bank as a Spectral Corpse when using {{il|Desecrate}} (up to 10 recent monsters), but spectres of [[Corpse item]]s and certain other monsters (e.g. [[Knitted Horror]]) cannot be desecrated this way. ==Gem level progression== {{Skill progression |c1_abbr = Maximum

Even for a non-summoner build, a single curse-casting spectre whose AI helps them stay away can be quite useful. Had powerful 50% [[chaos]] damage conversion attacks and an innate 67% damage reduction. ==Finding Spectres in Maps== Some guidance on Spectre corpse availability when raising Spectres in [[maps]]: *Maps have a selection from a default pool of monster types that will spawn, usually related to the [[tileset]]. *Certain map modifiers, usually containing the text {{c|mod|Area is inhabited by X}}, can entirely modify the pool of monsters that will appear in maps. *Some monsters that are normally only found in Tier 17 maps have a chance to appear in maps with the [[Invasive Adversaries]] [[Atlas Passive Skill Tree|Atlas passive]] allocated, allowing them to be accessed much earlier in mapping progression. *Players who already have monsters in their [[spectre bank]] will have 15% of their monster corpses replaced by [[Spectral Corpse]]s (100% in hideout). ==Spectre bank (spectre storage method)== {{main|Desecrate}} Players who may wish to obtain certain harder-to-obtain spectres from other players can do so by having other players use {{il|Desecrate}} (or alternatively, {{sl|Corpse Walk}} from {{il|Corpsewalker}}) while the desired spectre is in their spectre bank (a method of storing spectres for later sharing). Note that the spectre owner must be the one to use Desecrate; it is not possible for the other player to desecrate a monster that is not already in their pool, as spectres are not added to the area's monster corpse pool. After changes in [[version 3.25.0]], it is not possible to share spectres between characters on the same account, as corpses generated by characters are removed upon logging out of that character, where the term spectre bank originated from. However, reworks to Spectral Corpse generation and recent spectre memory largely mitigated the downsides of this change. It is still possible to create two accounts and run two instance of the game to share spectres. This requires Steam and standalone client of the game or running the standalone client with a secondary account in addition to the main, as well as alt-tabbing or dual monitors setup. ===Spectre channel=== Global [[Chat]] 6666 is a channel dedicated to spectre sharing with other players. Due to game population, this channel may only active in the current temporary trade leagues. ==Related unique items== The following [[unique item]]s are related to Spectres: {{Drop enabled unique item table |where = items.stat_text LIKE "%Spectre%" |large=1 |base_item=1 |level=1 |stat=1 }} ==Related mods== The following non-unique item mods are related to Spectres: {{modifier table |q_tables=mod_stats, mod_spawn_weights |q_join=mods._pageID=mod_stats._pageID, mods._pageID=mod_spawn_weights._pageID |q_where= ( (mod_stats.id LIKE "%spectre%" OR mod_stats.id LIKE "%spectres%") AND mod_spawn_weights.value > 0 AND mods.generation_type NOT LIKE "10" AND domain = 1 ) OR mods.id = "GlobalRaiseSpectreGemLevelUberMaven" |stat_text=1 |spawn_weights=1 |level=1 |generation_type=1 |group=1 }} ===Delve Drop-only modifiers=== The following mods are related to Spectres and only able to drop from specific Delve node: {{Modifier table |q_tables=mod_stats, mod_spawn_weights |q_join=mods._pageID=mod_stats._pageID, mods._pageID=mod_spawn_weights._pageID |q_where=(mod_stats.id LIKE "%spectre%" OR mod_stats.id LIKE "%spectres%") AND mods.domain=1 AND mods.generation_type=1 AND mods.name="Subterranean" |stat_text=1 |required_level=1 |generation_type=1 |group=1 }} ===Legacy mods=== ;Fossil-only modifiers The following mods are related to Spectres and only able to craft on item by using [[fossil]]. However such ability was removed from the fossil in [[version 3.10.0]]: {{modifier table |q_tables=mod_stats, mod_spawn_weights |q_join=mods._pageID=mod_stats._pageID, mods._pageID=mod_spawn_weights._pageID |q_where= (mod_stats.id LIKE "%spectre%" OR mod_stats.id LIKE "%spectres%") AND mod_spawn_weights.value > 0 AND mods.generation_type NOT LIKE "10" AND domain = 16 |stat_text=1 |spawn_weights=1 |level=1 |generation_type=1 |group=1 }} {{Skill enchantment modifier list|query=mods.generation_type=10 AND mods.stat_text_raw LIKE "%Spectre%"}} ==Spectre limit== By default, the player can summon only one Spectre at a given time at gem level 1. This limit can be increased with certain passive skills or items. ===Passive skills=== The following [[passive skill]] increase the player's Spectre limit: {{Query base passive skills |where=passive_skill_stats.id LIKE "%spectre%" }} ===Unique items=== The following [[unique items]] affect the player's Spectre limit: {{Drop enabled unique item table |tables=item_stats |join=items._pageID=item_stats._pageID |where=items.stat_text LIKE "%maximum number of Spectres%" |large=1 |stat=1 |level=1 }} ===Total=== Players can currently have a maximum of 25 permanent spectres at once: *3 from Level 25+ Raise Spectre (using + gem level equipment) *+1 from {{psl|Death Attunement}} *+2 from a max-rolled {{il|Eyes of the Greatwolf}} amulet with {{il|Carrion Queen Talisman}} enchantment *+1 from body armour (Delve drop-only prefix mod {{ml|MaximumMinionCountSpectreDelve}} or legacy {{il|Vis Mortis}}) *+2 from {{il|Queen's Decree}}, dual wielding {{il|Midnight Bargain}}, or using a single wand together with {{il|Bitterbind Point}} that has {{c|mod|+1 to maximum number of Spectres}} veiled modifier *x1.44 from a Level 5 {{il|Congregation Support}} (+1 from corruption, +1 from Elevated Elder or Redeemer body armour modifier) *x2 from {{il|The Dark Monarch}} Up to 6 additional temporary spectres can be gained by having {{il|Raise Spectre of Transience}} (or Raise Spectre with {{il|Soul's Wick}}) linked with a level 6 Congregation Support (Level 4 corrupted socketed to {{il|Honourhome}} or {{il|Viridi's Veil}}). ===Multiple raise spectre gems=== If you have multiple socketed Raise Spectre gems with different spectre limits (e.g. because one has a higher gem level, or is linked to {{il|Congregation Support}}) then each gem's own limit applies to spectres raised from that gem, and the maximum number of spectres you can have in total from all gems is the highest limit from any one gem. E.g. if you have one gem with a limit of 13 spectres and another with a limit of 10, you can have at most 13 active spectres in total, of which at most 10 can be raised using the gem with the limit of 10. {{Alternate skill effect list}} ==Version history== {{Version history table header}} {{Version history table row|3.29.0| * The audio for most Raised Spectres should now be quieter. * Lowered the Life of various Monsters when used as Spectres.
